fr:mainmatter.fr:p: While reading An Axiomatization of Set Theory, I just had the completely trivial-- and "that's… the point"-- "realization" that first order logic is the meta-language of axiomatic mathematics, just as (it seems) logical frameworks are the meta-languages of (typically λ-calculus based) programming languages. Well not literally, but the discrepancy is non-substantial.

That is, (classical) FoL is often the setting in which axiomatic mathematical theories are formalized. Classic (no pun intended) examples are ( \mathcal {L}_{group} = \{ e, ⋅, -⁻¹ \} , Th( \textsf {groups})), ( \mathcal {L}_{DLO} = \{ ≤ \} , Th( \textsf {Dense Linear Orders})), ( \mathcal {L}_{sets} = \{ ∈ \} , ZFC). (To be ultra-pedantic is a fruitless way, I've paired the language and theory.)
One of the early NBG papers. Maybe "the" NBG paper. My notes on this are currently in Variables Explained Away.
English translation in From Frege To Gödel.
